html:
The Ostrogoths were the eastern branch of the Goths, a Germanic people who in 493 founded a kingdom in Italy. The map shows them from 400 to 600.

In the 300s they lived on the steppe north of the Black Sea, where tradition remembers a great king, Ermanaric. The Huns overran them around 375, and for decades many served in Hun armies. After Attila died in 453 and his empire broke up, the Ostrogoths settled in Pannonia as allies of the Eastern Roman Empire.

Their king Theodoric the Great, raised as a hostage in Constantinople, was sent by Emperor Zeno to take Italy from Odoacer, the general who had deposed the last Western emperor. Theodoric killed Odoacer in 493 and ruled Italy from Ravenna until 526. He kept the Roman Senate and Roman law, employed Romans such as the philosopher Boethius, and ruled Goths and Romans side by side. The Goths were Arian Christians, the Romans Catholic.

After his death the kingdom weakened. In 535 Emperor Justinian sent Belisarius to retake Italy. The Gothic War dragged on for almost twenty years and ruined Italy. King Totila won back much of it, but he was killed at Taginae in 552, and Ostrogothic resistance was over by 554.
sum: The Ostrogoths were the eastern branch of the Goths, a Germanic people who in 493 founded a kingdom in Italy. The map shows them from 400 to 600.
